concept:
Create a polished ORIGINAL watercolor storybook level-design concept panorama for a tiny flame spirit puzzle platformer. Level 03, an old underground GARDEN DRAIN, following a terracotta-pot entrance. This is a new scene. Landscape very wide panoramic composition, ideally 2400x1000 or wider, full level left to right, SIDE-ON ORTHOGRAPHIC gameplay camera PERPENDICULAR to the rear brick wall. NOT isometric, not overhead, not a floating diorama. Foreground walkable silhouettes are crisp dark sepia ink outlined; subtle perspective is allowed only on non-walkable background surfaces. Quiet blue-gray masonry, warm brown bricks, desaturated jade moss, dangling fine roots, water stains, watercolor pigment granulation, beautiful hand-drawn fairy tale illustration, soft golden local light, paper texture. Avoid photorealistic CGI, industrial sewer machinery, giant boulders or excessive yellow saturation.
STRUCTURE: about 34 tiny-character heights long and 8 heights clear tunnel height, with foreground shallow water trough below discontinuous dry maintenance ledges. A low connector from the previous pot enters at far LEFT through a modest dark masonry doorway; the main drain is lower than the pot, which is outside the frame. No outdoor garden gate, no view of a whole pot. Brick vault and enclosing roots overhead. Foreground below the platforms: shallow blue water and damp recovery ledge, with short rubble steps allowing a fallen player to return, not a lethal abyss.
TRAVERSAL: a clear 2D route rising LEFT to RIGHT with nine discrete dry horizontal ledges. Left entry broad low dry ledge; two small hops lead to a broad operation terrace around x32%; then a short flat support around x42%; then five mossy broken brick / flat stone platforms rise in ~0.6–0.7 character-height steps across the right half, separated by short readable ~1 character-width gaps. Final broad landing high at right, containing a small outlet. NO unjumpably tall walls along the route, no spikes, no decorative ambiguous floating platforms. Each platform has a believable broken masonry buttress or corroded wall bracket.
ONE connected optical/mechanical puzzle at center-left:
1) Small antique garden maintenance lantern mounted UNDER the brick vault at x42%, y about upper20%, pointing STRAIGHT DOWN. Tarnished bronze casing, glass lens and a tiny amber seed of stored light inside, opened brass shutter. A thin black pull cord runs to a small accessible shutter control at the left entry terrace (x14%). The lantern is not held by the player.
2) Directly below the lantern at x42%, a small silvered reflector shard is held at a FIXED 45 DEGREE ANGLE, top-left to bottom-right (backslash in side view), on a vertically sliding old sluice carriage with two slender guides. The carriage has been raised into the upper position, around 65% up from the entry floor. It is NOT a passenger elevator. No rotation control, only height changes. Reflector about 1.2 times character height.
3) A taut hemp rope from the carriage goes over a visibly separate fixed pulley attached to the brick vault and back to a small ratcheting hand winch at x32% on the reachable operation terrace. Rope, wheel, guide and mirror need clear practical construction; no hanging rope crossing the light beam. Small rusty counterweight, restrained moss.
4) Draw exactly ONE correct L-shaped light path: narrow vertical golden beam DOWN from the lantern lens to the center of the suspended sloping mirror, then a narrow HORIZONTAL golden beam RIGHT from the mirror, passing ABOVE all the ascending platforms, ending on a single living feeding scale at the far-right wall. Do not make diagonal rays between source and mirror; no light through opaque bricks; no extra random beams. Beam should be about one character-height above the final landing.
RIGHT endpoint: only a small cropped section of the SAME enormous sleeping creature's TAIL ROOT emerges through old mortar above the last landing. Pearly ivory organic overlapping scales and a soft skin fold, not a gemstone or an egg or a boulder. Most body stays behind earth, NO face, eyes, legs or whole animal. One almond-shaped gold scale at beam endpoint glows. Beneath it, an existing modest masonry outlet toward the next garden watercourse is becoming accessible as a tiny tail fold relaxes upward; faint cool light, no outside panoramic view.
CHARACTER: exactly ONE very small glowing ivory light spirit at the hand winch, large round flame-shaped head, tiny body, short arms and feet, two dark oval eyes, about 1/32 scene width. Same soft nonhuman chibi spirit, no human coat or hat, no oversized protagonist. It remains a small presence within the drain.
Keep the scene uncluttered and hierarchy readable, darkest foreground roots framing bottom corners. Include only small neat ivory circular markers with the numerals 1 beside shutter control, 2 beside the winch, 3 near the rising platforms, 4 beside the feeding scale, 5 by the exit. No other text, no title, no UI, no motion arrows or phantom mirrors. This is the solved optical state of the level, a high quality art prototype scene not an infographic.
refinement:
Precise-object-edit of this existing watercolor drain level concept. Preserve the overall composition, camera, materials, brick vault, overall positions, L-shaped golden optical beam and numbered markers 1–5. Make only these practical gameplay corrections:
1. Shrink the single ivory flame spirit beside marker 2 to about 70 percent of its current height, preserving its feet on the winch terrace. It must feel tiny in this micro-world. Do not add another character.
2. Correct the rope topology: the HAND WINCH at marker 2 connects by a taut rope upward along the LEFT side of the fixed overhead PULLEY, wraps over the pulley, then descends on its RIGHT side and attaches to the TOP of the suspended MIRROR CARRIAGE. Show this continuous U-shaped load-bearing rope clearly, offset left of the golden vertical beam. The mirror carriage is the hanging load. Do not tie both ends of this pulley rope to two floor winches.
3. Marker 1 is a SMALL SHUTTER PULL LEVER for the lantern, not a second winch. Replace its large round wheel with a little bronze lever. Remove the existing strong diagonal rope from marker 1 to the pulley. Instead add a very thin dark shutter-control cord routed discreetly against the back wall and brick vault all the way to the LANTERN SHUTTER, bypassing the pulley entirely.
4. Make the jump route readable: add one narrow mossy brick stepping pier in the center gap directly BELOW the mirror carriage, midway between the winch terrace and the first right-hand platform; top level similar to winch terrace. Make its two remaining gaps about one tiny character width each. It must not obstruct the vertical lamp beam which ends well above it.
5. Along the ascending right-hand dry ledges, introduce FOUR genuinely open narrow gaps between successive mossy platform tops. Gaps roughly 0.7–1.1 character heights wide; each platform retains a broad flat top and believable masonry support. Preserve the progressive rise and final landing. Do not merely draw cracks in one continuous staircase; the player must need small jumps. No large impossible gaps.
6. Keep the shallow-water recovery area and show two small usable rubble steps leading back onto the left winch terrace, so a missed jump is recoverable.
Do not alter the main light ray: vertical DOWN from overhead lamp to the fixed 45-degree sloping reflector, horizontal RIGHT to the feeding scale, above the platforms. No added rays. Keep the tail-root patch only at upper right. Keep restrained watercolor ink style, not photorealism. No new text.
status: Concept proposal, not implemented Unity level.
